en.title: Number of Contiguous Combinations Whose Last Item Is Not the Maximum
en.description:
Following the source's enumeration, a combination means a non-empty contiguous subarray. A combination is balanced if its last item is not the maximum of the subarray, that is, some earlier number is strictly greater. Find the total number of balanced combinations; combinations may overlap.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. The original snapshot gives no value bounds; this site sets 1≤n≤200000 and elements in −10^9..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: [3,6,3] and [6,3] are balanced, 2 in total. Example 2: the last item of every segment is tied for the maximum and no element is strictly greater, so the answer is 0. Example 3: all three contiguous segments of length ≥2 are balanced, so the answer is 3.
hints: Maintain a monotonically decreasing stack of indices to find, for each last item, the position p of the nearest strictly greater value to its left; that last item contributes p+1 starting points.
